title: MeshDataTool, surface_remove and clear_surfaces not doing what I expect and corrupting ArrayMesh
body:
### Tested versions

Godot version: v4.4.1.stable.arch_linux (Compatibility renderer), haven't had the opportunity to test older versions of Godot.



### System information

Arch linux, Compatibility renderer, rtx 3070 on latest proprietary nvidia drivers.

### Issue description

_It's entirely possible this is a me-problem as I've only been using Godot for about a week, but I'm at a loss here._

I'm importing .gltf assets into my project (they are level scenes), and I'm using an EditorScript to do some pre-processing on these scenes.  The main thing I'm trying here is to modify the vertex colors on each mesh within that gltf scene (that has been instaniated into the godot scene), I'm using the MeshDataTool to do this and I'm getting really weird results when I combine it with surface_remove on the original mesh.   (My goal here is to bake a sort of fake AO effect based on where faces overlap by utilizing vertex colors)

I have a working version and a non-working version, the non-working version has me use MeshDataTool to create_from_surface for each surface in each ArrayMesh, I then remove the original surface from the mesh with surface_remove and add the new one from the MeshDataTool with commit_to_surface.  Note I have tried with clear_surfaces as well and seem to get the same results, the final mesh/scene when I load the game is just a mess and things are rendering weird (everything is in a weird position, down-scaled and going crazy)

Is this me misunderstanding how to use MeshDataTool?  I'm guessing not given that my second example seems to work fine?  I haven't been able to find much in the way of docs around modifying existing meshes using this method so this has taken me a while to figure out.



```
# This is the non-working version, world is the gltf scene dragged into the godot scene, I don't even bother to try and change vertex colors here because it just doesn't work at all
for N: MeshInstance3D in world.get_children():
	var mesh = N.get_mesh()
	if mesh is not ArrayMesh:
		continue
	print("Updating ArrayMesh")
	
        # (updated the range to be reverse as per clayjohn's reply below about the flawed logic here - issue persists)
	for s in range(mesh.get_surface_count() - 1, -1, -1):
		var mdt = MeshDataTool.new()
		mdt.clear()
		mdt.create_from_surface(mesh, s)
		mesh.surface_remove(s) # If I comment this out, it works but I end up with two overlapping surfaces per mesh, this and clear_surfaces specifically seems to break everything
		mdt.commit_to_surface(mesh) # I've tried having this before surface_remove, I've tried clear_surfaces instead, I've tried looping backwards over the surfaces in case it was some weird issue with the index, etc.
```

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/72225275-3ff9-40f4-be42-13c72779b932)



```
# This one seems to work fine, I create a new ArrayMesh and replace the original one with that, instead of using surface_remove.  
for N: MeshInstance3D in world.get_children():
	var mesh = N.get_mesh()
	if mesh is not ArrayMesh:
		continue
	print("Updating ArrayMesh")
	
	var new_mesh = ArrayMesh.new()
	var mdt = MeshDataTool.new()
	for s in range(mesh.get_surface_count()):
                mdt.clear()
		mdt.create_from_surface(mesh, s)
		for v in range(mdt.get_vertex_count()):
			mdt.set_vertex_color(v, Color(1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0))
		mdt.commit_to_surface(new_mesh)
	N.mesh = new_mesh
```

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3aecc298-c985-4c76-bca7-91a49366932f)


### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a gltf scene (I specifically used crocotile3d for the level scene)
2. Import into a godot scene
3. Use a gdscript tool/EditorScript to modify the vertices of each surface for each mesh in that instantiated gltf scene
4. use surface_remove and clear_surfaces to remove the original surface(s) from the mesh and commit to add the newly modified one, this seems to break everything, if I commit from the MeshDataTool without clearing the original surfaces then it doesn't break but I end up with two overlapping surfaces for everything in the scene 

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

I've not got a minimal reproduction project right now, not sure if/when I'll get the time to do that around my day job as I've already spent a lot of time this week on this bug/issue.
